objective: Create a polished visual brand-kit board for a lightweight web tool that finds scenic driving routes between two points. This is an implementable design target for a frontend designer or code agent, not a production raster UI asset. Preserve the map-first, single-task product character while defining a restrained modern system with subtle iOS-adjacent liquid-glass depth, without copying Apple or any reference brand.
deliverable_type: visual brand-kit board and product UI design-system specification
subject_content: A comprehensive but calm design-system board titled only SCENIC ROUTE — DESIGN SYSTEM for a scenic route-finding webapp: typography, named color swatches with exact hex values, spacing and grid, radii, borders, elevation, buttons, coordinate or place inputs, slider, checkbox, route-composer card, navigation or map controls, content containers, route and scenic-layer map treatments, icon and illustration direction, texture, and motion. Show one complete compact product example using the real route-planning interface and every required source string. Fit every module fully inside the canvas with comfortable edge padding.
required_text: No learned score for this tile
Avoid highways and major roads when possible
audience: Designers and frontend engineers building a small demonstration-quality scenic route planner for desktop and responsive web, with technical users able to enter coordinates.
visual_direction: Restrained, precise, map-first, outdoors-aware, and quietly premium. Use subtle liquid-glass principles only where useful: translucent graphite surfaces with dependable contrast, slight backdrop blur, a fine edge highlight, restrained elevation, and crisp controls. Keep the visual language lightweight rather than resembling a business dashboard. Avoid generic glossy AI/SaaS glassmorphism.
composition: One 1920×1080 editorial system board with a strong grid and immediate hierarchy. Include a compact title and design principles, primary and secondary typography specimens, named palette swatches with hex values, token strips for spacing/grid/radii/borders/elevation, a component family for buttons/inputs/cards/map controls, a small realistic scenic-route composer example, route and layer line-language samples, plus icon/image/texture/motion guidance. Generous negative space, readable labels, no mood-board collage.
color: Base the system on warm off-white map neutrals, deep graphite glass, a single distinctive mint or alpine green interaction accent, and restrained terrain-adjacent supporting hues. Route strokes must remain distinct from scenic-score overlays. Provide accessible text/surface contrast and exact named hex swatches.
typography: A contemporary humanist or neo-grotesk sans direction suitable for real web UI, with a slightly characterful display weight and highly legible UI/body styles. Specify primary and secondary typography direction, hierarchy, weights, sizes, and numeric treatment. No novelty display font and no copied brand typography.
materials_texture: High-opacity graphite translucent surfaces, modest blur, 1 px cool-light borders, subtle inner edge highlight, short soft shadows, and sparse topographic or contour-line texture used only as a quiet supporting motif. No heavy bloom, rainbow refraction, fake chrome, or nested glass cards.
reference_query: modern restrained map application interface editorial design system typography alpine terrain liquid glass product UI
positive_constraints: Treat the current full-viewport map and single compact route-composition surface as the product core.
Preserve start-to-end sequencing, one clear primary action, explicit detour multiplier, road-avoidance preference, service state, score state, and collapsed diagnostics treatment.
Use the exact visible strings only where UI examples need text; do not invent product claims, testimonials, pricing, navigation categories, or a brand name.

Define primary and secondary typography, named color swatches with exact hex values, spacing, grid, radii, borders, elevation, button, input, card, navigation or map-control, and content-container styling.
Include image, illustration, icon, texture, and motion direction plus concrete examples for this scenic-route product.
Keep all UI production-feasible with standard HTML, CSS, SVG icons, and common web-map capabilities.
Show strong keyboard-focus affordances, generous hit targets, and contrast that remains robust over a variable map.
Use references only for abstract visual qualities and create an original system.
negative_constraints: Do not copy logos, trademarks, layouts, or artwork from references.
Do not invent product claims or replace exact visible copy with marketing language.
Do not create a logo, invented brand name, tagline, descriptive product paragraph, fabricated route metric, duration, distance, score, place name, or unsupported control.
Do not crop any module, product card, label, motion guidance, texture guidance, or engineering note at the canvas edge.
Do not create a generic mood board, generic SaaS dashboard, corporate website, mobile-only UI, or fully built-out business application.

Do not use excessive neon, purple-blue gradients, nested transparent panels, microscopic labels, impossible shader effects, fake browser chrome, watermarks, signatures, or decorative controls that imply nonexistent functionality.
Do not make green route lines indistinguishable from scenic heatmap colors.
Do not obscure the map with a large opaque dashboard or persistent sidebar.
success_criteria: The board reads as one coherent, original visual system for a lightweight scenic route tool.
Every requested token and component category is visible, legible, and internally consistent.
Named swatches include usable exact hex values and typography direction is explicit.
Product examples preserve the current task hierarchy and use exact source copy where shown.
The generic heading reads SCENIC ROUTE — DESIGN SYSTEM; there is no logo, invented identity, tagline, fabricated metric, or unsupported product copy.
Every module and the entire realistic product example fit visibly inside the canvas with bottom and side padding.
Glass material is restrained, accessible, and feasible in responsive web UI.
The result scores at least 2 of 3 for purpose, hierarchy, composition, restraint, coherence, and production realism, with 3 for purpose or hierarchy.
No unintended watermark, copied trademark, illegible pseudo-copy in important labels, or map/UI technical artifact is present.
